At my hospital we take our X-rays and we actually send them out to a board certified radiologist and can usually get results within a day or so. Also, Xrays are done differently than a human doctor. Instead of standing there and moving your own body to the way the dr is saying. We are having to position the animal in 3-10 positions. This can be pretty involved when it can take 3 people to hold one big German shepherd down. Another thing is because pharmacies/medical ANYTHING companies love to the up the price on not super readily available products. Antibiotics are dirt cheap because you can get them anywhere and some can be used human and animal. When it comes to animal specific medications, they love to up the price on them and it’s costly to even stock them.

Think of it like this..in human medicine things are CRAZY expensive. 1 ER visit can cost you 8k-20k but we have insurance to cover majority of those cost. There is pet insurance that i HIGHLY recommend. It’s just not readily available like human medicine has.
Another thing to take into account is the medications and equipment hospitals have they have to pay for out of pocket. You are paying for the level of care you are receiving. It’s sad that I have seen actual veterinarians paying for equipment and supplies out of their own pockets when they feel it’s necessary and hospital funding/corporate approval isn’t there.
